front: State the 2020 ACC/AHA staging of primary MR.
back: Stage A: at risk (mild MVP, mild MAC). Stage B: progressive. Stage C1: asymptomatic severe with LVEF > 60% and LVESD < 40 mm. Stage C2: asymptomatic severe with LVEF ≤ 60% OR LVESD ≥ 40 mm. Stage D: symptomatic severe.

front: Class I indications for MV surgery in chronic PRIMARY severe MR?
back: 1) Symptomatic severe MR. 2) Asymptomatic severe MR with LVEF ≤ 60% or LVESD ≥ 40 mm. 3) Severe MR undergoing other cardiac surgery.

front: For chronic SECONDARY MR, when is transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER / MitraClip) indicated?
back: Persistent NYHA III–IV HF despite maximally-tolerated GDMT and CRT (if indicated), with severe secondary MR, LVEF 20–50%, LVESD ≤ 70 mm, and PASP ≤ 70 mmHg (COAPT-like criteria).

front: State the mitral regurgitation severity threshold for a positive PISA method requiring baseline shift.
back: Baseline shift lowers the aliasing velocity to ~30–40 cm/s. Do it in the DIRECTION of the jet (usually downward for MR viewed from apex).

front: How do you correctly grade an eccentric wall-hugging (Coanda) MR jet?
back: Do NOT use jet area or LA-area percentage — will underestimate. Use vena contracta width (severe ≥ 0.7 cm), PISA-derived EROA/RV, or volumetric SV-difference method.

front: Which valve maneuver increases the mitral prolapse murmur duration and moves the click earlier?
back: Valsalva strain phase (decreases preload) — smaller LV cavity causes earlier prolapse. Also standing. Increased venous return (squatting, leg raise) does the opposite (delays click, shortens murmur).

front: State three settings in which the pressure-half-time method underestimates MVA (overestimates severity).
back: 1) Stiff (non-compliant) LV. 2) Stiff LA. 3) Moderate-to-severe aortic insufficiency. 4) ASD. In all, PHT shortens due to non-MV mechanisms, not from valve disease alone.

front: How is prosthetic mitral valve stenosis identified on TTE Doppler?
back: E velocity ≥ 1.9 m/s, mean gradient ≥ 6 mmHg, VTI ratio (prosthesis/LVOT) ≥ 2.2, and PHT ≥ 130 ms. Use the continuity equation (not PHT) to calculate EOA.

front: Why does an eccentric wall-hugging jet appear smaller than a central jet on color Doppler?
back: The Coanda effect — as the jet adheres to the wall, kinetic energy is lost to friction, reducing the visible flow area. A wall-hugging jet may have 40% less color area than an equivalent central jet.

front: How do you distinguish mitral valve prolapse from billowing?
back: Prolapse: leaflet free edge ABOVE the mitral annular plane at end-systole with loss of coaptation. Billowing: leaflet body bulges above the annular plane, but the free edge remains at or below → coaptation preserved.

front: How does the exercise MR grade change help decide surgical timing in ischemic MR?
back: Exercise-induced increase in MR ≥ 1 grade or exercise EROA ≥ 0.13 cm² identifies patients with worse prognosis and may prompt earlier intervention.

front: After MitraClip, what causes recurrent MR at follow-up?
back: Single leaflet detachment (leaflet grasped only unilaterally), device embolization, progressive underlying disease. Recurrent MR sometimes requires additional clips or surgical intervention.
